title: High Sleep Duration Low Readiness Mismatch
dataSources: Apple Health metrics (`apple:health`), Oura Ring daily readiness/sleep (`oura:daily`), WHOOP recovery/strain (`whoop:cycle`), Withings body and blood-pressure (`withings:measure`), Dexcom CGM glucose (`dexcom:egv`).
app: Apple Health / Apple Watch exports (Health Auto Export, Shortcuts) via HEC; Oura, WHOOP, Withings, and Dexcom APIs via scripted REST inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily
| where sleep_hours>=8
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(readiness_score) as avg_readiness, count as long_sleep_days by user _time
| where long_sleep_days>=3 AND avg_readiness<70
| sort avg_readiness
description: Highlights weeks where you seem to be sleeping enough on paper but readiness remains low, a useful hint that quantity is not the real issue.
value: This catches the frustrating pattern where more time in bed still does not translate into feeling recovered, pushing you to inspect stress, illness, or sleep timing instead.
implementation: Forward sleep duration and readiness from Oura; review weekly when long-sleep weeks still carry poor readiness scores.
visualization: Weekly scatter plot of long-sleep days versus average readiness.
grandmaExplanation: It ranks when you are sleeping a lot but still waking up looking under-recovered according to the wearable.
